QUESTION: What condition on its quotient groups characterizes when a subnormal series of a group is a composition series?

ATOM: A subnormal series of a group is a composition series if and only if each of its quotient groups is simple and nontrivial.
KEY POINTS:
1. Every quotient group of the series is simple
2. Every quotient group is nontrivial (the series has no repetitions)

ANSWER TO GRADE:
A subnormal series is a composition series exactly when each of its successive quotient groups (factors) G_{i+1}/G_i is simple (and nontrivial, since the series is strictly descending). Equivalently, no proper nontrivial normal subgroups lie strictly between consecutive terms, so each factor has no normal subgroups other than the trivial ones.
